I'm curious if anyone else is a professional game dev by day and indie game dev by night and how they manage their time. I'm finding it difficult to split my time between dev, studies and social/spousal commitments. I seem to only be able to commit my whole focus to one area at a time.
Game dev by day, Game dev by night... How do you manage it?

I am in the exact same boat as you. I work as a professional dev in a studio during the day, and an indie/hobby dev at night while trying to raise a 6 year old whose going on 16.

It's tough, no two ways about it, and I frequently go with only 4-5 hours a sleep a night. A big part of it is having your friends and family (especially your wife if you have one) understand that it is a part of your life and you just can't ignore it.

Anyone who works as a professional dev knows that you never get a solid 8 hours of work in a day. By the time I'm done dealing with management, updating docs, meetings, and whatever else pops up you probably only get a solid 3-4 hours of work done in a single work day.

That 3-4 hours matches almost exactly the amount of time I try and accomplish at home in the evenings as well. In the early evening I take 20-30 minutes to plan out my work plan and get right to work on tasks. I break down things into as small as tasks as possible and go from there. My evening hours are never linear though. Very often I'll have to read a bedtime story, clean up a mess, take the dog out, etc, but I never let this work hold me back. I finish up whatever I'm going to do and get right back to work. It may not be perfect, but it's the best I can manage at the moment and it works pretty well, I make decent daily progress.

Thanks for the response. The fact that you are managing progress while raising a child as well truly impresses me.

I was also happy to get 2-4 hours per night Dev time so it is reassuring that you are expecting similar output. One thing I am pretty flaky at is planning my home work. I think I will try your method of planning the evening after getting home. Hopefully this helps.

Do you ever find yourself deep in multiple extra curricular projects and unable to chose where to devote your time?

All the time! I frequently get asked by friends and co-workers to lend a hand or to review something or the dreaded 'take a peek'. I have a hard time saying no, especially since I love the challenge of solving puzzles. I try and limit the help I give as much as possible, and I think most everyone I know understands that I'm pretty busy and have a lot on my plate. The only people I flat out refuse are the ones who want ridiculous tasks like creating a webpage or making a game for their kids(These ones always seem to have the 'next great idea').

Yes, learning to say no was very difficult for me. In the end it is the only fair answer most of the time. When it comes to after hours work I have found that I need to be selfish and do work that means something to me or else it just doesn't happen. Even then it is a struggle to pull myself up and make it happen sometimes.
